Short answer: In modern unified-memory GPUs, decoding latency for hybrid linear-attention (HLA) and full-attention (FA) models is dominated by how fast you can move tokens between LPDDR5X system memory, L2 cache, and the compute tiles that hold L1/shared memory. Bandwidth is the bottleneck; latency is a function of (tokens to fetch) / (effective bandwidth) plus small fixed overheads. HLA reduces the tokens you must fetch per step, so it directly cuts the bandwidth demand and thus the decoding latency.

Here’s a self-contained Python implementation of a bounded lock-free-style ring buffer simulator with producer/consumer backpressure metrics and unit tests.

Notes:
- “Lock-free style” here means:
  - Single-producer / single-consumer (SPSC) to keep it simple and correct without heavy atomics.
  - Uses a head/tail pointer scheme with wrap-around.
  - No Python-level locks; concurrency is simulated via cooperative scheduling.
- Backpressure metrics:
  - Producer: number of times it was blocked because the buffer was full.
  - Consumer: number of times it was blocked
